1. (Currently amended) A control system comprising: a controller including a processor and memory, the controller configured to be communicatively coupled to automation components in the control system and to facilitate performance of a process through interoperation with the automation components by generating a holistic state data structure stored in the memory, wherein the controller is configured to generate the holistic state data structure by: determining, using the processor, a mathematical model configured to describe the process used by the controller; determining, using the processor, input and output variables of the process; determining, using the processor, constraints on the input and output variables; determining, using the processor, an objective function associated with the process used by the controller; and storing, in the memory, the model, the input and output variables, the constraints, and the objective function in one of a plurality of fields in the holistic state data structure to enable the automation components to detect and operate with the controller upon receiving the holistic state data structure, wherein the holistic state data structure comprises a standardized data format that includes a model field, a variables field, a constraints field, and an objective function field.

2. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to be communicatively coupled to the automation components via a communication network and to communicate the holistic state data structure to each of the automation components upon connecting to the communication network.

3. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to be communicatively coupled to the automation components via a backplane and to communicate the holistic state data structure to the automation components upon connecting to the backplane.

4. (Previously presented) The control system of claim 1, wherein the holistic state data is a standardized format understood by each of the automation components.

5. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to generate the holistic state data structure by: determining, using the processor, an intermediate search result of an optimization search; determining, using the processor, a state of the optimization search when the intermediate search result is determined; and storing, in the memory, the intermediate search result and the state in an optimization state field of the holistic state data structure.

6. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to generate the holistic state data structure to facilitate performing an optimization search in conjunction with one or more of the automation components in the control system, wherein the optimization search uses the mathematical model, input and output variables, and objective function stored in the holistic state data structure.

7. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to generate the holistic state data structure by: determining, using the processor, computational capabilities of the controller; determining, using the processor, interconnections with the automation components in the control system; and storing, in the memory, the computational capabilities and the interconnections in a controller settings field of the holistic state data structure.

8. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller is configured to communicate the holistic state data structure to a server in the control system via the communication network to facilitate determining an optimization problem based on the model, variables, constraints, and objective function in the holistic state data structure.

9. (Currently amended) The control system of claim 1, wherein the controller comprises an in-memory database configured to store the holistic state data structure.

10. (Currently amended) A tangible, non-transitory computer-readable medium configured to store instructions executable by a processor of a controller, wherein the instructions comprise instructions to: receive, using the processor, control system configuration data comprising a plurality of holistic state data structures; determine, using the processor, automation components communicatively coupled to the controller and characteristics of the automation components based at least in part on parsing the control system configuration data; determine, using the processor, an optimization problem based at least in part on the automation components, the characteristics of each of the automation components, and the mathematical models, variables, and constraints contained in the holistic state data structures; and instruct, using the processor, one or more of the automation components to perform a control action in a process, wherein the control action is determined based at least in part on solving the optimization problem.

11. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the characteristics of each of the automation components comprise a model used by the automation component, wherein the instructions to determine the optimization problem comprise instructions to determine the optimization problem based at least in part on the model used by each of the automation components as contained in the holistic state data structures.

12. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the characteristics of each of the automation components comprise a computing capability of the automation component, wherein the instructions to determine the optimization problem comprise instructions to determine the optimization problem based at least in part on computing capabilities of each of the automation components as contained in the holistic state data structures.

13. (Previously presented) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the control system configuration data comprises a plurality of holistic state data, wherein each of the plurality of holistic state data corresponds with one of the automation components.

14. (Previously presented) The computer-readable medium of claim 13, wherein the instructions to determine the automation components and characteristics of the automation components comprise instructions to parse each of the plurality of holistic state data.

15. (Previously presented) The computer-readable medium of claim 13, wherein each of the plurality of holistic state data comprises a standardized format with same fields.

16. (Currently amended) The computer-readable medium of claim 10, wherein the instructions to receive the configuration data comprise instructions to receive the configuration data from a cloud-based server via a network connection.

17. (Currently amended) A method for performing diagnostics on a control system comprising: determining, using a processor, holistic state data structures captured by a controller in the control system, wherein each holistic state data structure comprises a mathematical model, input and output variables, constraints, and an objective function; simulating, using the processor, operation of the controller based at least in part on the holistic state data structures and the mathematical models contained therein while the controller performs other operations; analyzing, using the processor, the simulation of the controller to perform diagnostics on the controller by comparing simulated results with actual operational results; adjusting, using the processor, operation of the control system based at least in part on the diagnostics.

18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 17, wherein: simulating operation comprises simulating performance of various control actions by the controller using the mathematical models in the holistic state data structures; and analyzing the simulation comprises analyzing results of the various control actions and comparing the simulated results with actual results.

19. (Currently amended) The method of claim 17, wherein analyzing the simulation comprises: determining a predicted response to a control action determined by the controller using the mathematical model contained in the holistic state data structure; and comparing the predicted response with an actual response to the control action to determine accuracy of the mathematical model.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 19, comprising adjusting the mathematical model when the predicted response and the actual response vary by a threshold amount.
